title: Types of Bank Accounts in India: Features, Benefits and Key Differences
summary: Compare types of bank accounts in India, including savings vs current accounts, NRE vs NRO accounts, and fixed deposits vs recurring deposits.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


Bank accounts are your money’s first home. They secure your money while also supporting you in managing your savings or investments.


In today’s world, not having a bank account is unthinkable, whether you are employed, a student, an entrepreneur, a partner in a partnership firm, or a non-resident Indian. Bank accounts have become an essential aspect of every person’s life.


Individuals in India can open a variety of bank accounts for a range of purposes. Without further ado, let us explore the different types of bank accounts in India.


### TL;DR


- Savings accounts support personal saving and everyday spending. Current accounts are designed for business transactions.
- Fixed deposits hold a lump sum for a chosen term, while recurring deposits build savings through regular instalments.
- NRE and NRO accounts hold rupees. FCNR(B) accounts hold permitted foreign currencies as term deposits. Eligibility, tax treatment and repatriation rules differ.


##


Types of Banks That Offer Bank Accounts in India


Some of the main categories of banks in India are listed below.


1. Private banks
2. Public-sector banks, including nationalised banks
3. Foreign banks
4. Cooperative banks


You can open a bank account with banks in these categories, subject to their eligibility and account requirements. Other categories include small finance banks and payments banks.


##


Main Bank Account Types in India


Customers can open various kinds of accounts in more than one bank as per their requirements. The different types of bank accounts and their features are explained below.


### Savings Account


The phrase is self-explanatory. It implies that these bank accounts are intended for individuals to save money. Eligible Indian residents can open a savings bank account by completing the[KYC requirements for opening a bank account](https://www.rbi.org.in/commonman/Upload/English/FAQs/PDFs/KYC09062025.pdf) . Aadhaar is one accepted identity document.[PAN](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/PAN-verification/) or the applicable declaration is also required.


**Key features**


- For this type of bank account, most regular accounts have no general cap on the amount deposited, subject to KYC, product limits and reporting requirements.
- Depending on your bank, the total number of transactions may be regulated in some instances
- In most circumstances, a customer is obliged to maintain a mandated minimum balance to keep the savings account open, unless it is a zero-balance product
- When the obligatory minimum balance criterion is not applicable, there are various exceptions. Let’s say you opened a savings account via the government’s financial inclusion scheme, called the “Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana,” in which case there is no minimum balance requirement. Basic savings bank deposit accounts provide at least four free withdrawals per month under RBI’s rules. Digital payments other than ATM transactions are excluded from that count.
- When it comes to interest, a customer gets interest on savings account deposits. This interest rate differs from one bank to another
- Savings accounts are the most convenient way to generate interest on dormant money in banks


### Current Account


Current accounts are typically used for everyday business activities wherein funds are regularly transferred between bank accounts. These accounts are suitable for[everyday business transactions](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/business-banking/) by businesses and corporate officers.


The majority of current accounts are under the names of[corporations or enterprises](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/corporate-account/) . These accounts are intended for day-to-day business payments. The account holder can make withdrawals subject to the bank’s limits and available funds.


The bank does not pay interest on these accounts and instead may charge these account holders for other services.


**Key features**


- Current accounts support frequent transfers, but transaction limits and charges depend on the bank, account product and transfer channel.
- The minimum balance of a current account is often greater than that of a savings account.
- Customers do not earn interest on their current accounts
- If you’re wondering what the advantage of a current account is, it may offer an overdraft option, subject to approval. These accounts allow their customers to withdraw more money from the bank than is actually in the account, within the sanctioned overdraft limit
- In general, a minimum balance is intended to be maintained at all times. Daily limits, cash-deposit allowances and charges depend on the bank’s terms

It is a payment platform customised for your requirements that allows you to[collect payments](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-gateway/) ,[make payouts](https://www.cashfree.com/payouts/) ,[handle international payments](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/global-payment-apis-crossborder-collections-and-payouts/) , and do much more. These[APIs](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/overview) offer integration options and will help your business scale as it grows.


### Salary Account


Salary accounts are typically used by companies to credit employees’ salaries. These bank accounts are opened as part of a collaboration between the bank and the employer of a company or industry.


Each employee gets paid depending on the employer’s payroll disbursements. It is a more simple and more convenient option for crediting the employee’s account.


**Key features**


- When we talk about benefits, the salary account is beneficial not just to the company but also to the employee. A salary account generally has no minimum balance requirement while it qualifies for salary-account benefits
- The account holder can earn interest on the money in the account, with the interest rate determined by the kind of bank account
- If the salary has not been deposited into the employee’s account for three months, the account may be turned into a regular savings account, depending on the bank
- The account may thereafter require a minimum balance to be maintained. If the bank allows it and your company has a relationship with that bank, you can convert your savings account back to a salary account
- Transfer limits in this kind of bank account depend on the bank and payment channel. Employees can conduct[independent transfers](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/imps-vs-neft-vs-rtgs/) between one type of bank account and another


### Recurring Deposit Account (RD Account)


These accounts are often referred to as RDs, which can provide a higher interest rate than savings accounts, depending on the bank and deposit term.


Recurring deposit accounts are beneficial for people who do not have a large amount of money but wish to save a small chunk of their earnings each month. The recurring account has a preset duration. The account holder deposits a predetermined sum of money into the account usually on a monthly basis.


These accounts are suitable for long-term savings if an individual wishes to save funds for a child’s schooling, marriage, and so forth.


**Key features**


- The initial deposit required to open an RD depends on each bank. Customers can open an RD account with their preferred bank and make regular deposits. The minimum monthly deposit varies by bank
- Some banks additionally permit customers to deposit a greater number of payments up to a certain limit
- On the scheduled day of the month, the instalment is deposited into the RD. If the customer decides to withdraw the money prior to the expiration date, a penalty may apply in the form of a lower interest rate
- This account’s most versatile feature is that it allows users to save money for periods that may range from six months to ten years, depending on the bank, and earn interest on the amount deposited
- RD accounts can also be closed before the term comes to an end subject to the bank’s premature-closure terms and applicable interest adjustments


### Fixed Deposit Account (FD Account)


FD Accounts are another name for Fixed Deposit Accounts. In this type of account, a set amount of money is placed in the bank for a defined period.


These accounts are created in order to receive interest on deposits for a specific time period until maturity. Fixed deposits are generally considered low-risk deposit products for saving and earning interest on idle funds.


With a standard lump-sum FD, the individual deposits the funds once and receives the proceeds at maturity. For callable fixed deposits, the user can usually withdraw before the term specified at the time of deposit expires, with an interest adjustment or penalty. Lock-in and withdrawal conditions depend on the product.


**Key features**


- The maximum amount that may be invested into a fixed deposit account depends on the bank and product. The greater the money allocation, the greater the interest paid after the account’s duration
- Banks pay interest on FD accounts, albeit the percentage differs from bank to bank. The Fixed Deposit Account commonly has terms ranging from 7 days to 10 years, depending on the bank and product
- Furthermore, the rate of interest on the fixed amount invested in the account will differ slightly based on the time duration of the FD selected by you
- Fixed deposits are generally low-risk investments. Due to the fixed-term benefits that a bank has with FDs, several banks in India provide FD interest rates that are greater than savings accounts. RD interest rates may be similar for comparable terms
- Banks may retain large funds for a defined duration of time, while customers can earn predetermined returns, making the financial instrument a win-win for both banks and consumers


##


Savings Account vs Current Account


**Feature** **Savings account** **Current account**


Main purpose Personal savings and everyday spending Frequent business transactions


Interest Usually pays interest Generally does not pay interest


Minimum balance Depends on the product, with zero-balance options available Depends on the bank and account product


Overdraft Available only with specific facilities or products May be available with the bank’s approval


##


Fixed Deposit vs Recurring Deposit


**Feature** **Fixed deposit (FD)** **Recurring deposit (RD)**


How you save Deposit a lump sum Deposit regular instalments


Useful when You already have money to set aside You want to build savings over time


Interest Depends on the amount, term and bank Depends on the term and bank


Early closure Subject to product restrictions and applicable interest adjustment Subject to bank terms and applicable interest adjustment


##


NRI Bank Account Types: NRO, NRE and FCNR(B)


Banks in India provide a variety of bank accounts and services to Indians and Indian-origin people living abroad who want to open a financial bank account in India. NRI accounts are classified into three categories:


### NRO Account


- A non-resident ordinary bank account is another name for an NRO account. NRO accounts are rupee accounts, which implies they keep deposits in Indian rupees
- The funds deposited can include earnings in India and permitted foreign remittances. This bank account serves to convert foreign currencies into Indian rupees
- Interest earned in these accounts is generally taxable in India, and the individual can create an NRO account in forms such as a savings account, a current account, a fixed deposit, or an RD, depending on his requirements. This account can also be formed jointly with another eligible person under the applicable rules
- Any amount of the balance can be kept, subject to the bank’s terms and foreign exchange rules


### NRE Account


- A Non-resident external account is another name for an NRE account. An eligible non-resident Indian can open this account. On becoming non-resident, an existing resident savings account generally needs to be redesignated as NRO
- Permitted foreign currency deposits in this type of account are converted into Indian rupees at the current rate of exchange. In India, the interest collected on these bank accounts is not taxable. The exemption depends on meeting the applicable residency and account conditions
- A prospective change in the currency rate has an impact on these accounts. The NRI can use the NRE account to open a savings account, a current account, or even a fixed deposit account
- Interest earned on the principal amount is exempt from Indian income tax when the applicable conditions are met. The benefit of this account is that permitted deposits can be held in rupees and the principal and interest are repatriable


### FCNR(B) Account


- An FCNR Account is a foreign currency non-resident account. This account pays interest, which is exempt from Indian income tax subject to the applicable conditions. These accounts keep savings in the currency authorised by India’s central bank, the Reserve Bank of India
- An eligible NRI or person of Indian origin can keep deposits in a recognised currency through which they generate their earnings
- If the revenue is produced in a currency different from those on the authorised list, a permitted currency is chosen for the conversion of the profits or funds to be deposited.
- FCNR bank accounts are sometimes referred to as FCNR (B) accounts, where the ‘(B)’ refers to banks. Through the FCNR account, an NRI can only create a fixed deposit bank account with a term of one to five years, subject to the bank’s deposit terms


##


NRE vs NRO Account


**Feature** **NRE account** **NRO account**


Currency Indian rupees Indian rupees


Main purpose Hold permitted overseas earnings and other eligible credits Manage Indian income and other permitted credits


Interest tax treatment in India Exempt when applicable conditions are met Generally taxable


Repatriation Principal and interest are repatriable Current income can be remitted after tax compliance. Other eligible balances may be remitted up to USD 1 million per financial year, subject to conditions.


The RBI’s guide to accounts for non-residents explains the permitted credits, account forms and repatriation conditions.


##


Which Type of Bank Account Should You Choose?


These are the most common types of bank accounts in India. Banking in India is tailored to various age groups and genders by both public and private financial institutions, allowing all residents to become financially empowered.


The interest rate on money saved in the bank varies depending on the kind of account and the bank itself. Therefore, before investing your money in bank accounts, you should familiarise yourself with the details of each type of bank account.
